delta.common_mechanics: The check/tick/send_packet/emit_page/read_safe code is byte-identical after JSON type normalization. A new read_active function and revised29-check main replace the baseline28-check metadata scenario.
delta.new_coverage: Two same-producer/same-context metadata reservations with distinct tickets and RO readers; cancellation of A while B and producer pages remain ACTIVE; actual late INSTALL(A) server error and another B ACTIVE observation; producer release followed by B/producer SAFE and retained A SAFE; all three actual reader closes.
delta.retained_prior_coverage: This scenario does not repeat the baseline cross-version/idempotent ACQUIRE, explicit VirtualQuery protection, wrong-generation reader rejection, or one-phase v2 INSTALL rejection checks. Those remain prior-case evidence rather than claims of this29-check run.

assessments.topic: Distinct actual reservation owners and immutable identity
assessments.result: The client uses an actual owned Root and actual self birth/session, ordinary USER96-v2 QUERY/ACQUIRE, and the same producer identity. Two successful PREPARE replies supply nonzero tickets; CHECK12 requires distinct increasing tickets. A and B have separate owned reader pointers opened using the same full producer identity and context_id1 but their respective tickets. read_active requires a valid non-SAFE ACTIVE snapshot, the expected ticket and lease, and the intentionally zero permission-only sequences. Full other immutable fields remain bound by the unchanged status-reader identity validation.

assessments.topic: A cancellation does not supply B terminal permission
assessments.result: Both pages must initially be ACTIVE. CANCEL targets only ticket_a with a fresh sequence. CHECK16 requires an actual A SAFE_ONLY read with safe1 and invalid dynamic values. CHECK17 then requires B ACTIVE under ticket_b; CHECK18 separately requires the producer page ACTIVE under ticket0. A real INSTALL_PREPARED_HOST packet is sent only after A SAFE and must return authoritative ERROR_INVALID_HANDLE; CHECK20 observes B ACTIVE again. SAFE, mismatch, invalid, or exhausted reads cannot satisfy read_active.

assessments.topic: Producer release collects the remaining reservation
assessments.result: The client sends no CANCEL for B. The next mutating control is a fresh-sequence producer RELEASE. It then requires actual B SAFE, actual whole-producer SAFE, and another A SAFE read while all three local views remain owned. Closing A, B, and producer happens only after those checks; each close must actually succeed and clear its reader owner. Writer-side disappearance therefore is not substituted for a retained-view SAFE read.

The inherited sender rejects undelivered, uncorrelated, malformed, or late replies and never automatically replays a control. PREPARE requires successful status and a real ticket; only CANCEL and RELEASE admit actual SUCCESS/IO_PENDING, followed by independent page proof. A failed primary check prevents29/0 even if cleanup succeeds. Failure cleanup closes each owned reader independently and destroys only the owned Root/class, without replaying unknown PREPARE/INSTALL outcomes. Partial NT reader owners remain available to the inherited close retry mechanism.

read_active checks its four-second monotone QPC budget after emitting result-change records, retries only READ_RETRY, and rejects other non-snapshot outcomes. The inherited SAFE poll and USER send preserve their budgets, including the post-JSON send check. I/O failure, nonzero cleanup result, incomplete checks, or any failed check prevents success. All29 numbered checks are present.

report.admission_scope: Admit this same-process normal metadata/page isolation client relative to the admitted metadata v2 basis, using unchanged qualified helpers and paired transport/header binding. Context_id1 is metadata only; no usable reserved ticket is installed before cancellation.
limits: Only the two named client files were read in this review. Previously admitted page-reader/transport/server mechanics supply context; helper/server source, build products, controller, dependency closures, and runtime receipts were not re-audited or independently rebound.
No code edits, builds, tests, candidate execution, network, runtime control, or Windows/default changes. Only this requested report was written.

No actual29/0 result, strict both-PE compile result, paired artifact identity, cleanup restoration, or runtime admission is claimed. Parent must bind these sources to the qualified unchanged helpers/header/transport.

ACTIVE assertions establish actual page snapshots at the specified observation points, not continuous liveness or a fresh installed/quiescent acknowledgement. All-zero dynamic sequences remain permission-only. Ticket uniqueness is checked for A versus B within this run.

Only READ_SNAPSHOT records qualify ACTIVE assertions, and only SAFE_ONLY with invalid values qualifies terminal permission. Nonready/error record payloads are not independent identity/value evidence; the inherited logging behavior was not used to qualify them.

Elapsed guards reject late completion after return but cannot preempt blocked USER/NT/output or window/class cleanup calls. An external controller watchdog remains necessary. Failure-path cleanup=true reports local close/window cleanup and is not by itself whole-server drain evidence after an unknown reservation/acquisition.

This case does not provide a CAContext/model/render/GPU/pixel, cross-process, NT-close-failure, concurrent-CANCEL, fault-injection, or negative-control qualification. It does not replace blocked acceptance. No blocked partial files or parked cross-process preparation were accessed, resumed, or retried.
